title: Pacific or Alaskan Cod, Frozen, Wild Caught

content.title: About
content.content: Cod (Gadus macrocephalus) is a marine fish from the cod family, inhabiting the cold waters of the Pacific Ocean along Alaska and Canada. Wild‑caught and flash‑frozen immediately after harvest, it retains its fresh taste and nutritional qualities.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cod can grow over 1.5 m long and weigh more than 30 kg.
Wild‑caught cod is considered more sustainable than farmed due to strict quota management.
Cod is low in fat but rich in omega‑3 fatty acids EPA and DHA.
Traditional Alaskan Indigenous dishes, such as “potapik,” feature cod cooked with berries.
Flash‑freeze technology preserves over 90 % of vitamins and minerals.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3 supports heart health, reduces inflammation, and promotes brain function.

items.title: Low calorie content
items.content: 100 g of cod provides about 80 kcal, making it a great choice for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Cod supplies roughly 18 g of complete protein per 100 g, essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is vital for nervous system health and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Contains selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as a powerful antioxidant protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, including cod.

items.title: Potential heavy‑metal exposure
items.content: While wild cod generally has low mercury levels, a varied diet is recommended.

items.title: Proper thawing required
items.content: Improper thawing can lead to bacterial growth and affect flavor.

items.title: Added sodium in processed products
items.content: If cod is sold as a seasoned or pre‑cooked product, check the sodium content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cod can be baked, pan‑seared, steamed, or added to soups and stews. Thaw it completely in the refrigerator, rinse, and pat dry before cooking. Serve with lemon, herbs, and vegetables for a light, nutritious meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen cod in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Once thawed, use within 1–2 days and store in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C. Do not refreeze.
